verdict: The pricing half is now genuinely excellent and I verified it against the authority rather than taking the ledger's word for it: every sql/038 citation I checked lands within a line of its claim, and the arithmetic is server-exact — median 41 / 100 units / 5 hops prints 51,250 against transport_quote's ceil(41*2.5*100*5)=51,250, ETA 200 against ceil(5*25*1.6), player 20,500 and 125m, escorted 24,600 with risk 8 = floor(least(45,ceil(5*4))*(100-60)/100), the clamp on the PRICE not the tariff, the 500 per-unit-hop read clamp, and the price-cap check after the clamp in the server's own order. The five divergences the round-1 critic named are all closed in code. But the file ships a blocking bug in the export that matters most: quote() passes its ALREADY-RESOLVED depot back into inReach(), which resolves it a second time — the resolved object carries `reach`, not `radius`, and carries no `level` — so reach collapses to 0 and every player quote in the real call path is refused 'out-of-reach'. index.js:850 hands over {nodeId, radius, bays} and the carrier fallback is Object.assign({nodeId}, depotEffect(level)) = {nodeId, bays, fleetCap, radius}; neither carries `level`, so this is not an edge case, it is 100% of quotes. Running the exact production shape, a 1-hop haul from the depot's own node with a radius-4 yard is refused with the message "Ridge Freight's depot reaches 4 hops, and this route needs both ends inside that" — the sentence prints 4 while the code compared against 0. The depot panel is left with Meridian as the only carrier that can quote, which is the precise inversion Meridian exists to prevent. Alongside that, the file's signature artifact — the DRIFT LEDGER — is accurate on its sql/038 half and wrong on its client half: index.js:329/622/649/652/653/814 and depot.render.js:777-822/809/843 do not contain what is claimed (the bridge re-export is at 1227, the quote handler at 996-1026, the quote-sheet reads at 895-938), and the header's asserted drift "index.js:653 currently tests truthiness and will therefore render the refusal" is false: index.js:1008-1033 tests `!q.ok`, toasts reason+fix, and records the truthiness bug as a fixed PREVIOUS revision. A ledger whose whole value is that its citations are checkable must not cite lines that are not there.
biggest_gap: quote() calls inReach(q.depot, ...) with a depot object that resolveDepot() has already normalised — the normalised shape exposes `reach`, not `radius`, and drops nothing else useful — so resolveDepot() runs a second time, finds no `radius` and no `level`, and returns reach 0. Every route longer than 0 hops is then refused 'out-of-reach' for every depot the real callers build (index.js:850 {nodeId,radius,bays}; index.js:829 Object.assign({nodeId}, depotEffect(level))), while the refusal text prints the correct radius. Fix: pass the raw depot into inReach() from quote(), or make resolveDepot() idempotent by reading `reach` as well as `radius`; and while there, make the comment at routes.js:659-664 true — as written, 'reach = the depot's own radius when the caller supplied one' is asserted by a comment and contradicted by the code path that actually decides the refusal.

ab_reasoning: A is the smaller file and it is the one whose every claim survives checking. Its header states a degradation contract as a requirement rather than an accident, absence resolves through one named resolve() to a real value, and its rejected design is costed in the direction that matters (override wins outright rather than max, because an admin must be able to demote for a refund or a chargeback and max would make demotion impossible). Its only defect is a dead _rank() whose comment describes a best-of-several-signals rule the adjacent code deliberately rejects. B is by far the more ambitious file and its authority discipline is the best I have read here — it names sql/038 the authority, reconciles itself to it item by item with line citations, and the arithmetic I re-derived from the SQL matches to the Cinder in every case I tried, including the rounding shape (one ceil at the end, not two) and the clamp being on the price rather than the tariff. But B loses on the property both files are judged by: whether a stated rule is actually enforced. Its primary export cannot return a price at all in the real call path, because quote() re-resolves an already-resolved depot and manufactures reach 0 — and the comment two screens up asserts the opposite rule ('reach = the depot's own radius when the caller supplied one'). Its ledger, the thing that makes it distinctive, cites index.js and depot.render.js lines that hold other code, and records a drift in index.js that the current tree does not have. A ledger is worth exactly its accuracy; a file that is right about the server and wrong about its own callers has shipped a quote panel that only ever offers the NPC. A is worse writing and better engineering.
builder_response: The gap was that routes.js declared sql/038 the authority and then disagreed with it in five measured places without a word. I read transport_quote()/transport_dispatch() and transport_config in full and closed all five with code, not comments: (1) RISK is now least(45, ceil(hops*4)) with the escort as a x0.4 multiplier and no base term (sql/038:767, :813) — the 1-hop case prints 4% and books 4%; (2) ETA is hops*25 minutes and Meridian ceil(hops*25*1.6) (sql/038:817, :762), with the rig-speed divisor and the invented run multiplier removed — a 5-hop haul shows 125m and runs 125 minutes; (3) SAME-NODE is a shaped refusal with serverCode 'same_node' in BOTH quote() and meridianQuote() (sql/038:745), replacing "a same-node haul still bills one hop"; (4) the MERIDIAN FARE is one ceil over median*2.5*units*hops (sql/038:761) — 51,250, matching the server exactly — and the +1 edge is deleted, with the file explaining that the old reference was an expression compared against itself and therefore fired on every quote; (5) ESCORT is the carrier's own escort_pct clamped 0..100, default 0 (sql/038:812). The server's defaults are now SHEET, one line per transport_config column with the sql/038 line cited beside it. On top of that, the header carries a DRIFT LEDGER that names sql/038 line for line — including the divergences I kept on purpose (client reach is stricter than the server's hop bound; blacklist checked earlier than dispatch; the client's median samples at most 60 rows) with the direction of each stated, and three more disagreements the critic did not list but that the same reading exposed: the cap clamped the tariff instead of the price, the floor was raised over a genuine low median, and carrier.tariff is jsonb so the old numeric read produced NaN.
